detailed_description: The File Size Calculator converts a storage value across common byte units in the browser. Enter a value, choose the source unit, then switch between binary 1024-based conversion and decimal 1000-based conversion. The page shows equivalent byte-unit values from B through PB, bit-based equivalents, and the total byte count. It is useful for comparing operating-system style binary sizes with storage-manufacturer decimal sizes when planning uploads, estimating package sizes, checking media files, or explaining why the same file size may appear differently across tools.
usage_steps: Enter the file size value in the input field.
Choose the source unit: B, KB, MB, GB, TB, or PB.
Select Binary for 1024-based units or Decimal for 1000-based units.
Review the byte conversion list for equivalent values in each unit.
Check the bit conversion panel for bits, kilobits, megabits, and gigabits.
Use the total bytes value when you need a normalized byte count.
usage_examples: Convert 1 GB using binary mode to see the byte count an operating system may use.
Switch to decimal mode to compare a storage-device size against manufacturer units.
Estimate how many megabytes or gigabytes a media file represents before upload.
Convert a package size to total bytes for a technical note or test case.

faqs.question: What is the difference between binary (1024) and decimal (1000) units?
faqs.answer: Binary units use base-2 (1 KiB = 1024 Bytes), commonly used by operating systems like Windows and Linux. Decimal units use base-10 (1 KB = 1000 Bytes), standard for hard drive manufacturers and networking.

faqs.question: Which storage units are supported?
faqs.answer: The calculator converts between Bytes (B), Kilobytes (KB/KiB), Megabytes (MB/MiB), Gigabytes (GB/GiB), Terabytes (TB/TiB), Petabytes (PB/PiB), and bit equivalents.

faqs.question: Can I convert from bits to bytes?
faqs.answer: Yes. The results panel automatically displays bit-based equivalents (bits, kilobits, megabits, gigabits) alongside byte-based storage units.
